cases.title: Self-hosted LLM inference at scale with per-team quotas

defects: Two separate single-zone PAI-EAS nodes (llm-a zone A, llm-b zone B) instead of one multi-zone service or a note that EAS dedicated groups span zones; acceptable as explicit failover design but slightly over-specified.
NAT edge labeled for PAI-EAS to pull images/call APIs is fine, but weights-in-OSS (the usual pattern) is not mentioned in narration or diagram.
Narration does not mention autoscaling or router/prefill-decode separation in the why texts, which the guidance expects described for scale to 2,000 concurrent users.
reasons: Covers the core ask: AI Gateway for per-team quotas and failover in front of PAI-EAS Qwen endpoints in Singapore, with observability via SLS and Prometheus.
Placement follows the rules: SLS and Prometheus drawn outside the VPC as regional services, ALB and gateway multi-zone as single nodes, no DNS hop, no prices.
Draw-first behavior is correct: assumptions shown as chips and two design-changing questions (model size, warm vs cold standby) with quick replies.

cases.title: EU-only training data and large distributed training (no Lingjun in Frankfurt)

defects: Lingjun node placed in Frankfurt region; catalog says Lingjun's only international region is Singapore, so this violates the EU-only constraint and is not available there
Narration never states that Lingjun is unavailable in Frankfurt nor offers the fallback (DLC on general GPU pools, GPU ECS, or ACK)
No discussion of GPU availability for 30B training in Frankfurt; A100/H100-class GPUs are not offered internationally, making the training design likely infeasible as drawn
DLC->Lingjun edge labeled 'control' while Lingjun->CPFS carries the data path; training-to-storage data flow via CPFS is not shown directly
reasons: Lingjun is not offered in Frankfurt (Singapore is its only international region) and the answer places it in Frankfurt without flagging this
A 30B multi-node training job needs A100/H100-class GPUs which are never offered internationally on EAS/DLC public pools; this feasibility gap is not mentioned
Otherwise complete and readable: OSS+CPFS+DLC+EAS+Gateway in Frankfurt with sensible edges and good questions

cases.title: Flip the single-region assumption to two regions

defects: GTM -> dns edge is backwards/pointless: GTM itself is the DNS steering layer; keeping both Cloud DNS and GTM with users->gtm(resolve) then gtm->dns muddles the resolve path.
ESA has no origin/failover path to the Tokyo ALB, so if Singapore fails the edge layer cannot reach the DR region; GTM steering to a region ESA cannot reach is broken.
CEN and both Transit Routers are isolated nodes with only control edges to each other; they never attach to either VPC, so the private cross-region link is decorative.
DTS is placed as a node inside the Singapore region group; it should be a sync link between db and db-dr, not a regional resource.

Turn-2 narration does not mention CEN/private connectivity or how ESA fails over, and repeats the turn-1 questions that were never answered instead of asking about active-active vs active-standby or RPO/RTO.
reasons: Two-region DR added correctly with GTM, DTS and a full standby stack, and the single-region chip is gone.
DNS/GTM wiring is confused: users resolve via GTM but GTM->dns edge and the leftover Cloud DNS node make the entry path unclear; ESA is not connected to the Tokyo origin.
CEN/TR nodes are dangling (control edges only, no VPC attachments) and DTS is drawn as a node in the Singapore region rather than a link between the databases.

cases.title: Alibaba Cloud object storage only, as a backup target for AWS

defects: Express Connect shown as a hop writing to OSS; OSS is a regional service outside the VPC reached via its endpoint, not through the VPC boundary device.
Cloud Backup node added without need: it backs up ECS/NAS/OSS/VMware, not AWS workloads, so it cannot manage AWS-to-OSS backup jobs.
No mention of how AWS data actually lands in OSS (S3-compatible tools, DTS, or third-party backup software), leaving the core flow unexplained.
Versioning/cross-region backup options for OSS not considered despite being the natural fit for a backup target.
reasons: Correctly keeps everything on AWS as one other-cloud node and adds only OSS on Alibaba Cloud, with a stated region assumption and one relevant connectivity question.

Placement and data-path defects: Express Connect is a VPC boundary service, but OSS is regional and reached via its endpoint, so the ec->oss 'write' edge through the VPC is misleading; Cloud Backup is an unnecessary extra node for a simple AWS-to-OSS backup target.
Narration is clear and concise, but the diagram would need fixes (drop Cloud Backup or justify it, fix the OSS path) before signoff.
